title: Nudge and keep
objectives: Improve one weight by trying a small nudge each way and keeping the better one.

screens.title: Which way?
screens.prose: Start from the worst line, $y = 0x + 0$, with MSE 38.2. You may change $w$ by 0.1 only.
screens.question: Which plan should the rule follow?

options.text: Try both 0.1 and −0.1 and keep the better
Add 0.1: the points go up
options.why: That guess is right here, but a rule cannot rely on looking. Trying both always works.

options.text: Take 0.1 away
options.why: That moves the line further below the points. Only trying would tell you; trying both does.

options.text: Neither: 0.1 is too small to matter
options.why: Small changes add up over many rounds.

hints.text: Without a picture, how would you know which way is better?
Work out the MSE both ways and compare.

feedback.correct: Try both ways and keep whichever lowers the MSE.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Think about a rule that needs no picture.

byKey.up: Your eye is right here, but the rule we want works without a picture: try both and compare.

explain.text: A rule that tries both directions and compares the MSE needs no picture. That is the idea of this lesson.

screens.title: Try both
screens.prose: The slider moves $w$ to −0.1, 0 or 0.1 with $b$ kept at 0. The caption shows the MSE.
screens.question: What is the MSE at $w$ = 0.1?

hints.text: Slide to 0.1 and read the caption.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Set the slider to 0.1 and read the MSE.

explain.text: At $w$ = 0.1 the MSE is 34.23; at $w$ = −0.1 it is 42.39. The step up lowers the error, so we keep it.

screens.title: Nudge and keep
screens.prose: That is the **nudge rule**: try a small step each way and keep the one that lowers the error most. If neither does, stay put. Next comes $b$, from $w$ = 0.1, $b$ = 0 (MSE 34.23).
screens.question: $b$ = 0.1 gives MSE 33.14 and $b$ = −0.1 gives 35.34. What is $b$ after this nudge?

hints.text: Which of the two is below 34.23?
33.14 is lower, so keep $b$ = 0.1.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Keep the trial with the lower MSE.

byKey.down: 35.34 is higher than 34.23, so that nudge is rejected.
byKey.stay: One nudge does lower the error, so we move.

explain.text: 33.14 is below 34.23, so the rule keeps $b$ = 0.1. The line is now $y = 0.1x + 0.1$.

screens.title: One round, by hand
screens.prose: A **round** is one nudge of $w$, then one nudge of $b$. Here is the whole first round from (0, 0), which started at MSE 38.2.
screens.question: Fill in the last column: is each trial kept?

hints.text: A trial is kept only if it is the lower of its pair and below the error before it.
yes, no, yes, no.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Compare each pair with the error before it.

explain.text: $w$ + 0.1 beats 38.2 and its partner, so it is kept (34.23). Then $b$ + 0.1 beats 34.23 and its partner (33.14). After round 1 the line is $y = 0.1x + 0.1$.

screens.title: Fifteen rounds of moving
screens.prose: Repeat rounds until a whole round changes nothing. The bars show the MSE at the start and after each round that moved the line.
screens.question: After which round does the MSE first fall below 1?

hints.text: Read the bars from the left until one is below 1.
Round 12 leaves 1.24.
Round 13 leaves 0.50, the first below 1.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Find the first bar below 1.

byKey.before: After round 12 the MSE is 1.24, still above 1.
byKey.after: Round 14 leaves 0.12, but round 13 already got below 1, at 0.50.

explain.text: The MSE falls every round, fast at first; round 13 takes it from 1.24 to 0.50, the first value below 1. It reaches 0.06 after round 15. Round 16 finds no nudge that helps, so the rule stops at $y = 1.5x + 1.3$.

screens.title: It must move
screens.prose: At $w$ = 1.5, $b$ = 1.3 (MSE 0.06): $w$ ± 0.1 both give 0.17, and $b$ ± 0.1 both give 0.07.
screens.question: What does the nudge rule do in this round?

options.text: Nothing: every nudge raises the error, so it stays
Moves $w$ to 1.6: a round must change something
options.why: A nudge is kept only if it lowers the error. Moving to 0.17 makes the line worse.

options.text: Moves both $w$ and $b$ up by 0.1 to try something new
options.why: The rule nudges one number at a time and keeps only what helps.

hints.text: Is any of the four below 0.06?
No: 0.17 and 0.07 are both higher, so nothing changes.

feedback.correct: Nothing changes, so the rule stops.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Compare each nudge with 0.06.

byKey.move: You kept a nudge because it moved. It raised the error from 0.06 to 0.17. The rule keeps only a lower error.

explain.text: Every nudge raises the error above 0.06, so the round changes nothing. That is how the rule knows to stop.

screens.title: The size of the step
screens.prose: The same rule run with three step sizes, each from (0, 0).
screens.question: Why does step 0.01 stop at 0.0608, above the 0.06 that step 0.1 reached?

options.text: From (1.48, 1.36) every single nudge raises the error
A smaller step always gives a worse line
options.why: Step 0.5 stopped at 0.1, worse than 0.0608. Smaller is not always worse.

options.text: It ran out of rounds before reaching 0.06
options.why: It stopped because no nudge helped, not because of a round limit.

options.text: 0.0608 is the best line for step 0.01
options.why: Moving $w$ up and $b$ down together reaches 0.0606, lower.

hints.text: All four single nudges are above 0.0608; moving $w$ up and $b$ down together gives 0.0606.

feedback.correct: Each single nudge raises the error, though moving both together would lower it.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Check what the rule can try at (1.48, 1.36).

byKey.best: You took the stop for the best line. A move of both numbers at once reaches 0.0606, lower.

explain.text: At (1.48, 1.36) the four single nudges give 0.0611, 0.0627, 0.0609 and 0.0609, all higher. Moving $w$ up and $b$ down together gives 0.0606, but the rule never tries that. “The error stopped falling” means no single nudge helps, not that this is the best line.

screens.title: One round in code
screens.prose: Here is the rule exactly. Try $w$ + step and $w$ − step; if either lowers the MSE, keep the lower (the + step if they tie). Then the same for $b$, starting from the new $w$.
screens.question: Write `nudge_once(w, b, xs, ys, step)` that does one round and returns `(w, b)`.

widget.how: Check runs 8 hidden tests. Each pair is accepted when both numbers are equal to the expected ones up to a tiny rounding difference.

mutants.symptom: A tie counts as an improvement, so the line moves when it should stay.
Judges the b nudge as if w had not moved this round.

hints.text: Work out `best = mse(w, b, xs, ys)` first.
Compare `up` and `down` with `best` before you change `w`.
Use `if up < best and up <= down:` then `elif down < best:`; repeat for `b`.

feedback.correct: Your round tries each number both ways and keeps only what lowers the error.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Read the first failing test.

byKey.test-2: From (1.5, 1.3) nothing should move. If yours moved, you kept a nudge that did not lower the error.
byKey.test-3: Here $w$ is already right and only $b$ should move, to 1.0.

explain.text:
Each number gets two trials, and a trial wins only if it beats the current error.

```python
if up < best and up <= down:
    w, best = w + step, up
elif down < best:
    w, best = w - step, down
```

screens.title: The rule in words
screens.prose: Learning by nudging: $$\text{try } w \pm \text{step, keep the lower if it lowers the MSE; then the same for } b$$ and repeat rounds until a round changes nothing. Then no single nudge helps. That is not the same as being the best line.
screens.question: A round from some $(w, b)$ changes nothing. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Each of the four single nudges gives an error no lower than now
No line through these points has a lower error
options.why: Step 0.01 stopped at 0.0608 while 0.06 exists. A move of both numbers can still help.

options.text: The error has reached exactly 0
options.why: The rule stopped at 0.06 on our points, not 0.

options.text: The step was too big to find the best
options.why: Step 0.1 stopped at the best line. Stopping says nothing about the step being wrong.

hints.text: What does the rule check in a round?
It tries $w \pm$ step and $b \pm$ step and keeps only a lower error.

feedback.correct: Only the four single nudges are ruled out.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Think about what a round tries.

byKey.best: You read the stop as the best line. It only means no single nudge of this size helps.

explain.text: A round tries four single nudges. If it changes nothing, none of them lowers the error. Other moves, or other steps, may still do better.

screens.title: Tuning a trading rule
screens.prose: A fund trades when its signal is above a cut-off. Each week it tries the cut-off 0.05 higher and 0.05 lower on the past year. It keeps whichever made more money.
screens.question: What is the danger in that weekly nudge?

options.text: It is scored on the same past year it is tuned on, as in l4
0.05 is far too small a step to matter at all
options.why: Small steps add up over many weeks. The danger is what the steps are scored on.

options.text: Trying both directions each week wastes time
options.why: Trying both is what makes the rule work without a picture.

options.text: None: it is the nudge rule, so it is safe to use
options.why: The rule only lowers the error on the data it sees. That data also scores it.

hints.text: Which data choose the cut-off, and which score it?
The same past year does both.

feedback.correct: Same rule, same danger: tuned and scored on the same past.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Ask which data the result is judged on.

explain.text: The weekly nudge is exactly our rule, with profit in place of MSE. It keeps whatever looked best on the past year, which is a training score. Only days kept back can show whether it works.

ideas: The nudge rule tries a small step each way and keeps the one that lowers the error, else stays.
A round nudges $w$, then $b$; rounds repeat until a whole round changes nothing.
Stopping means no single nudge helps, not that the line is the best: step 0.01 stops at 0.0608 although 0.06 exists.

formula.name: One nudge
formula.tex: w \to \begin{cases} w + s & \text{if } \mathrm{MSE}(w + s) < \mathrm{MSE}(w) \text{ and } \mathrm{MSE}(w + s) \le \mathrm{MSE}(w - s) \\ w - s & \text{if } \mathrm{MSE}(w - s) < \mathrm{MSE}(w) \text{ and } \mathrm{MSE}(w - s) < \mathrm{MSE}(w + s) \\ w & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}

summary.trap: Keeping a nudge because it moved: a nudge is kept only if it lowers the error.
